## F3P1: Total number of EdU+ cells in lakritz mutants and wild-type siblings
```{r, echo=FALSE}
F3P1EdULakritz<-read.csv("/Users/cervenyk/Documents/fish data/Tectum_Hannah_Mate_collaboration/firstpass_figures for tectum paper/Figure_3_EdU/TectumF3P1_EdULakrtiz.csv")
View(F3P1EdULakritz)
```
### Part 1 Plot to look at distribution of data
```{r, echo=FALSE}
#first factor data into levels by age and genotype
F3P1EdULakritz$dpf<-factor(F3P1EdULakritz$Age,
                           levels=c("5 dpf", "7 dpf", "9 dpf"))
F3P1EdULakritz$Genotype<-factor(F3P1EdULakritz$Genotype,
                                levels=c("WT", "lak"))
#make boxplot
TectumF3P1_EdULakritz <- ggplot(F3P1EdULakritz, aes(x= Genotype, y= Total))+
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA)+
  geom_jitter(color = "black", fill = "gray", pch=21, size = 2, alpha=0.7, width=0.3)+
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("black", "gray"))+
  facet_wrap(~Age, strip.position = "top", scales = "free_x")+
  scale_x_discrete(labels=expression(WT, italic(lak)))+
  xlab("Genotype")+
  ylab("Total Number of EdU+ Cells")+
  ylim(0, 450)
print(TectumF3P1_EdULakritz)
```
###F3P1 Statistics
```{r, echo=FALSE}
#To prep for Summary Statistics (n, mean, median, SD)
group_by(F3P1EdULakritz, Genotype, Age) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(Total, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(Total, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(Total, na.rm = TRUE))
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
#Specify 5 dpf
F <- F3P1EdULakritz$Age == "5 dpf"
F3P1EdULakritz[F,]
#Specify 7 dpf
S <- F3P1EdULakritz$Age == "7 dpf"
F3P1EdULakritz[S,]
#Specify 9 dpf
N <- F3P1EdULakritz$Age == "9 dpf"
F3P1EdULakritz[N,]
```
#checking data for normality and equal variance (and inspecting for even distribution of samples per category)
```{r, echo=FALSE}
#most parametric assumptions = random representative collection, appropriate sample size, normal distribution (Shapiro–Wilk test vs Q-Q plots), and homogeneity of variance 
with(F3P1EdULakritz[F,], shapiro.test(Total[Genotype == "WT"])) #p-value = 0.1001
with(F3P1EdULakritz[F,], shapiro.test(Total[Genotype == "lak"])) #p-value = 0.03237     *
with(F3P1EdULakritz[S,], shapiro.test(Total[Genotype == "WT"])) #p-value = 0.6206
with(F3P1EdULakritz[S,], shapiro.test(Total[Genotype == "lak"])) #p-value = 0.06655
with(F3P1EdULakritz[N,], shapiro.test(Total[Genotype == "WT"])) #p-value = 0.3033
with(F3P1EdULakritz[N,], shapiro.test(Total[Genotype == "lak"])) #p-value = 0.003257    *
#p-value > 0.05 implies that the distribution of the data are not significantly different from normal distribution.
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
qqnorm(F3P1EdULakritz[F,]$Total, pch = 1, frame = FALSE)
qqline(F3P1EdULakritz[F,]$Total, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
qqnorm(F3P1EdULakritz[S,]$Total, pch = 1, frame = FALSE)
qqline(F3P1EdULakritz[S,]$Total, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
qqnorm(F3P1EdULakritz[N,]$Total, pch = 1, frame = FALSE)
qqline(F3P1EdULakritz[N,]$Total, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Variance Testing
# F-test is very sensitive to departure from the normal assumption. If there is doubt about normality, the better choice is to use Levene’s test or Fligner-Killeen test, which are less sensitive.

fligner.test(Total ~ Genotype, data = F3P1EdULakritz[F,]) #p-value = 0.2269
fligner.test(Total ~ Genotype, data = F3P1EdULakritz[S,]) #p-value = 0.3207
fligner.test(Total ~ Genotype, data = F3P1EdULakritz[N,]) #p-value = 0.102
#p-value > 0.05 implies that the variances are not significantly different from each other
```

##For stats for analysis and adding p-values to plot, choose generalized linear model (negative binomial but with dispersion since variance is very variable when comparing ages) glmmTMB
```{r}
F3P1EdULakritz$Genotype <- factor(F3P1EdULakritz$Genotype, levels = c("WT", "lak"))
F3P1EdULakritz$Age <- factor(F3P1EdULakritz$Age)

# 1. Fit the Negative Binomial Model (Safely absorbs biological overdispersion)
mod_EdUlakAgeCount <- glmmTMB(Total ~ Genotype * Age, dispformula = ~ Age, family = nbinom2, data = F3P1EdULakritz)

summary(mod_EdUlakAgeCount)

#g_null <- update(mod_EdUlakAgeCount, . ~ 1)              # check summary(g_null) still supports using dispersion model
g_add  <- update(mod_EdUlakAgeCount, . ~ Genotype + Age)

#anova(g_null, mod_EdUlakAgeCount)      # overall LRT
anova(g_add,  mod_EdUlakAgeCount)      # interaction LRT
AIC(mod_EdUlakAgeCount)

#In the output, this is the line that matters for the overall model: 
#mod_EdUlakAgeCount  9 923.92 946.41 -452.96   905.92 8.8597      2    0.01192 *
#(chi^2(df) = value, p = value)

emm_EdUlakAgeCount <- emmeans(mod_EdUlakAgeCount, ~ Genotype | Age, type = "response")
summary(contrast(emm_EdUlakAgeCount, "revpairwise", by = "Age"), adjust = "holm", by = NULL, infer = TRUE)

emm_EdUlak_ALL <- emmeans(mod_EdUlakAgeCount, pairwise ~ Age | Genotype, type = "response")
summary(emm_EdUlak_ALL$contrasts, adjust = "Holm", by = NULL)
```
## Now remake plot with relevant stats added
```{r, echo=FALSE}
stat_manual_lakEdU <-tibble::tribble(
  ~Age, ~group1,~group2,~p.adj,
  "5 dpf", "WT", "lak", 0.999,
  "7 dpf", "WT", "lak", 0.999,
  "9 dpf","WT","lak", 0.0028
) %>%
  mutate(
    dpf = factor(Age, levels = c("5 dpf", "7 dpf", "9 dpf")),
    p.adj.signif = case_when(
      p.adj < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p.adj < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p.adj < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE          ~ "ns"
    ),
    y.position = 435   # adjust based on your error bar heights per facet
  )

#Now make box plot with stats
TectumF3P1_EdULakritz_stats <- ggplot(F3P1EdULakritz, aes(x= Genotype, y= Total))+
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA)+
  geom_jitter(color = "black", fill = "gray", pch=21, size = 2, alpha=0.7, width=0.3)+
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("black", "gray"))+
  facet_wrap(~Age, strip.position = "top", scales = "free_x")+
  scale_x_discrete(labels=expression(WT, italic(lak)))+
  xlab("Genotype")+
  ylab("Total Number of EdU+ Cells")+
  ylim(0, 450)+
   stat_pvalue_manual(stat_manual_lakEdU, label = "p.adj.signif", 
                     xmin = "group1", 
                     xmax = "group2",
                     y.position = "y.position")
print(TectumF3P1_EdULakritz_stats)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
ggsave("TectumF3P1_TectumF3P1_EdULakritz_stats.png", TectumF3P1_EdULakritz_stats, path=NULL, 
         scale = 1, width = 14, height = 10, units = "cm", dpi = 300, limitsize = TRUE, bg=NULL)
```

### F3P2: Ratio of EdU+ cells in intact and one-eyed brains
```{r, echo=FALSE}
HannahEdUEnuc5dpf<-read.csv("/Users/cervenyk/Documents/fish data/Tectum_Hannah_Mate_collaboration/firstpass_figures for tectum paper/Figure_3_EdU/TectumF3P2_HannahEdUEnuc5d.csv")
View(HannahEdUEnuc5dpf)
```
## Make plot to view the data before doing stats
```{r, echo=FALSE}

                              levels=c("7 dpf", "9 dpf"))
HannahEdUEnuc5dpf$Innerv<-factor(HannahEdUEnuc5dpf$Innerv,
                                 levels=c("intact", "one-eyed"))
```


### F3P2 Stats
```{r, echo=FALSE}
#Summary Statistics (n, mean, SD)
group_by(HannahEdUEnuc5dpf, Innerv, dpf) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(Ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(Ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(Ratio, na.rm = TRUE))
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
#Specify 7 dpf
S <- HannahEdUEnuc5dpf$dpf == "7 dpf"
HannahEdUEnuc5dpf[S,]
#Specify 9 dpf
HannahEdUEnuc5dpf[!S,]
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
#Check Data before t-test
#T-test assumptions: random representative collection, appropriate sample size, normal distribution (Shapiro–Wilk test vs Q-Q plots), and homogeneity of variance 
with(HannahEdUEnuc5dpf[S,], shapiro.test(Ratio[Innerv == "one-eyed"])) #p-value = 0.4428
with(HannahEdUEnuc5dpf[S,], shapiro.test(Ratio[Innerv == "one-eyed"])) #p-value = 0.4428
with(HannahEdUEnuc5dpf[S,], shapiro.test(Ratio[Innerv == "intact"])) #p-value = 0.95
with(HannahEdUEnuc5dpf[!S,], shapiro.test(Ratio[Innerv == "one-eyed"])) #p-value = 0.1621
with(HannahEdUEnuc5dpf[!S,], shapiro.test(Ratio[Innerv == "intact"])) #p-value = 0.2201
#p-value > 0.05 implies that the distribution of the data are not significantly different from normal distribution.
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
qqnorm(RouseTUNEL[X,]$Ratio, pch = 1, frame = FALSE)
qqline(RouseTUNEL[X,]$Ratio, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
qqnorm(RouseTUNEL[S,]$Ratio, pch = 1, frame = FALSE)
qqline(RouseTUNEL[S,]$Ratio, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
qqnorm(RouseTUNEL[N,]$Ratio, pch = 1, frame = FALSE)
qqline(RouseTUNEL[N,]$Ratio, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Variance Testing
# F-test is very sensitive to departure from the normal assumption. If there is doubt about normality, the better choice is to use Levene’s test or Fligner-Killeen test, which are less sensitive.
# However, we will be using Welch's t-test which assumes unequal variance!
var.test(Ratio ~ Innerv, data = HannahEdUEnuc5dpf[S,]) #p-value = 0.1517
var.test(Ratio ~ Innerv, data = HannahEdUEnuc5dpf[!S,]) #p-value = 0.001038    *
#p-value > 0.05 implies that the variances are not significantly different from each other
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
#Hedges test for 7 dpf
hedges_g(Ratio ~ Innerv, data = HannahEdUEnuc5dpf[S,])
#Hedges test for 9 dpf
hedges_g(Ratio ~ Innerv, data = HannahEdUEnuc5dpf[!S,])
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# 1. Fit a standard Gaussian GLM
HannahEdUEnuc5dpf$Innerv <- factor(HannahEdUEnuc5dpf$Innerv, levels = c("intact", "one-eyed"))  
HannahEdUEnuc5dpf$dpf <- factor(HannahEdUEnuc5dpf$dpf, levels = c("7 dpf", "9 dpf"))
fit_innervEdU <- gam(Ratio ~ Innerv * dpf, 
                  family = gaussian(link = "identity"), 
                  data = HannahEdUEnuc5dpf)

# 2. Check the Model Summary
summary(fit_innervEdU)
anova(gam(Ratio ~ 1, data = HannahEdUEnuc5dpf), fit_innervEdU, test = "F")   # overall test statistic

# 3. Pairwise post-hoc tests with Bonferroni-Holm adjustment
pairwise_results_innervEdU <- emmeans(fit_innervEdU, pairwise ~ Innerv | dpf, type = "response")
summary(pairwise_results_innervEdU$contrasts, adjust = "Holm", by = NULL)

# View the adjusted p-values
#pairwise_results_innerv$contrasts

```

## Now remake plot with relevant stats added
```{r}
stat_manual_EdUInnerv <-tibble::tribble(
  ~dpf, ~group1,~group2,~p.adj,
  "7 dpf", "intact", "one-eyed", 0.091,
  "9 dpf","intact","one-eyed", 0.0001
) %>%
  mutate(
    dpf = factor(dpf, levels = c("7 dpf", "9 dpf")),
    p.adj.signif = case_when(
      p.adj < 0.0001 ~ "***",
      p.adj < 0.001 ~ "**",
      p.adj < 0.01  ~ "*",
      p.adj < 0.05  ~ "",
      TRUE          ~ "ns"
    ),
    y.position = 0.65   # adjust based on your error bar heights per facet
  )

#Now make box plot with stats
TectumF3P2_HannahEdUEnuc5d <- ggplot(HannahEdUEnuc5dpf, aes(x= Innerv, y= Ratio))+
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA)+
  geom_jitter(color = "black", fill = "gray", pch=21, size = 2, alpha=0.7, width=0.3)+
  facet_wrap(~dpf, strip.position = "top", scales = "free_x")+
  xlab("Innervation Status")+
  ylab("EdU Ratio [(L-R)/Total]")+
  ylim(-0.15,0.68)+
  stat_pvalue_manual(stat_manual_EdUInnerv, label = "p.adj.signif", 
                     xmin = "group1",
                     xmax = "group2",
                     y.position = "y.position")

print(TectumF3P2_HannahEdUEnuc5d)
```
